defects.description: Race condition: The token decrement 'self.tokens -= 1' occurs outside the thread lock. Multiple threads can concurrently pass the 'if available >= 1' check after releasing the lock, leading to a negative token count and allowing more requests than the configured capacity.

Rate drift: Setting 'self._last = now' discards the fractional remainder of time that didn't constitute a full token. This causes the effective refill rate to be slower than the configured 'rate', especially when 'allow()' is called frequently at intervals just over the token period.

Non-monotonic clock: 'time.time()' is used to measure elapsed time. If the system clock is adjusted backwards, the limiter will stall and stop accruing tokens until the clock catches up to the 'self._last' value. 'time.monotonic()' should be used for rate limiting.

obvious_bugs: State mutation (decrementing tokens) happens outside the critical section protected by the lock.
notes: The code represents a common but flawed implementation of the Token Bucket algorithm. The concurrency bug is a 'textbook' example of a check-then-act race condition.
